Your roll after this.","private_thought":"Built StC+States 3h\u21924h ($200). Pinks 4/4/4 ($625/$625/$700), oranges already 4/4/4 ($750/$750/$800). p2 liquidity is ~$545 (7 red houses\u00d7$75 + $20), so any pink or orange hit bankrupts them. Bank left with 1 house; p2 has $20 and cannot buy it unless I pay a red on the doubles re-roll (Ky/In 2h $250, Ill 3h $750; 15/36). Do not hotel \u2014 returns 4 houses. Next: consider soaking the last house via LB unmortgage (all 3, $176) + 1 house ($50) only if still legal; otherwise end. Do not trade Park Place/orange/pink/GOOJF or give cash. Do not unmortgage yellows/rails/utils. Cash after build ~$1418 covers any current red."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I rolled doubles and landed on ST_JAMES_PLACE. I have $1618 cash, two GOOJF cards, and three houses left in the bank. I am deciding what post-turn action to take.

I own five properties with 3–4 houses each. MEDITERRANEAN_AVENUE and MARVIN_GARDENS are unmortgaged and unbuilt. The opponent has $20 cash and is on NEW_YORK_AVENUE after paying rent. p3 and p4 are bankrupt.

The opponent cannot afford houses. I will build evenly on the pinks to reach 4/4/4. The bank now has 3 houses.

Hoteling would return four houses to the bank, but the opponent cannot afford them. After landing on ST_JAMES_PLACE, the next doubles roll could land on Tennessee Avenue, New York Avenue, or Free Parking.

I mapped the remaining doubles outcomes. The next roll could land on Kentucky, Indiana, or Illinois. All three are owned by the opponent with two to three houses. I am checking standard rent values for those properties.

I confirmed the opponent's red properties are worth $250–$750. I can pay any of those rents easily. I am weighing whether to build houses now or wait, since the opponent could eventually buy them if they collect rent.

I calculated the opponent's worst-case scenario. If they collect $770 from rent, they could buy five houses with only three available. That would raise their reds to 3/3/4. I would have $868 left after paying $750 for Illinois rent. That might cover the $925 rent on Illinois if I land there again.

I decided to buy houses now. Building two pinks from three to four will empty the bank and prevent the opponent from ever building there, even if they collect rent. Hoteling would return four houses to the bank, which is dangerous if the opponent ever gets cash. Virginia Avenue is already at four houses.

I will build two houses on ST_CHARLES and STATES to reach 4/4/4. One house will remain in the bank. The opponent could buy it for $150 if they collect rent, but that would leave them with only $120.

Hoteling would return four houses to the bank, worsening the housing situation. I am now considering unmortgaging yellow properties like ATLANTIC and VENTNOR to build on them instead.

I checked the light blue monopoly. All three properties are mortgaged, so I would need to pay $176 to unmortgage them first. Building one house on each would cost another $150, bringing the total to $326. That is a lot of cash to spend on a single color group.

I am now considering the light blue monopoly. Unmortgaging all three properties and building one house each would cost $326, but it would lock every remaining house in the bank. That prevents the opponent from ever buying a house again, even if they collect rent. The rent on those properties is very low, so the cost may be worthwhile.

I checked the opponent's mortgaged properties. Unmortgaging Pacific, Pennsylvania, Boardwalk, and the PA railroad would cost $671 total. Even with $750 collected from rent, they could only afford two of those properties. North Carolina Avenue is unowned, so they cannot complete a green monopoly.

The opponent cannot complete a dark blue monopoly without my Park Place, so the reds are their only buildable group. Emptying the bank is therefore the winning move. I can only perform one post-turn action, so I must choose between building on the pinks or unmortgaging the light blues.

Unmortgaging the light blues requires three separate actions. I am now verifying standard Monopoly rent values for the pink properties to confirm the exact threat of reaching 4/4/4.

Official rent values confirm the pink threat. St. Charles and States each jump from $450 to $625 per house, and Virginia is already at $700. Building two pinks consumes two of the three remaining houses. One house still needs to be taken.

I realized the even-build rule allows a one-house difference, so I can place one house on a single light blue property without unmortgaging the others. I am now checking whether building is permitted on a mortgaged property.

Standard Monopoly rules confirm that building is impossible on a mortgaged color group. All three light blue properties must be unmortgaged before any house can be placed there. That costs $176, and adding one house would cost another $50. The rent gain from one house on those properties is only $50 to $60, so the total investment of about $226 may not be worthwhile.

I am weighing the $226 cost of unmortgaging the light blues against the value of locking one house. The opponent would need to land on a red property to buy that house, and from St. James Place there is only about a 42% chance of hitting a red on the next doubles roll.

I am now calculating the exact expected value of spending $226 to lock one house. If I hit a red this turn, the opponent could buy that house and later raise rent from $250 to $700. I am also considering what spaces the opponent can reach from NEW_YORK_AVENUE on their next roll.

I mapped the opponent's next roll from NEW_YORK_AVENUE. They could land on Kentucky, Indiana, or Illinois. All three are owned by them with two to three houses. Marvin Gardens is unmortgaged but lacks a yellow monopoly because Atlantic, Ventnor, and Water Works are mortgaged. The rent there would be only $24.

Marvin Gardens rent is only $24, but the opponent has only $20. They would need to sell a red house for $75 to cover it, leaving them with $71. That still does not cover the $150 cost of buying a house.

The opponent's next roll mostly lands on their own or mortgaged properties, so they will not collect cash from rent. I must act before my re-roll, which is the post-turn action after moving but before ending the turn. Building two houses on St. Charles and States now costs $200 and leaves one house in the bank. This locks the pink monopoly at 4/4/4, which is clearly positive expected value.

I can afford the opponent's highest red rent even if they upgrade to three houses. Their cash is only $20, so they cannot rebuild. I will not spend $226 to lock the last house.

The opponent can raise only about $545 from selling houses and cash. That is enough to pay a $750 rent on St. James Place, so one hit there would bankrupt them. I am now verifying the exact orange rent values.

Official orange rent values confirm the threat. A single hit on a four-house orange property would cost $750 to $800, which exceeds the opponent's $545 liquidity. The same is true for a four-house pink property at $625. Their total liquid assets are only $545, so they cannot pay even one of these rents.

I will build one house on both St. Charles Place and States Avenue in a single build_plan call. I am now considering whether to trade.

function.name: end_turn
function.arguments: {"public_message":"Still standing. Reds are waiting for you. Your roll.","private_thought":"Still standing. Reds are waiting for you. Your roll."}
